# M3 donor catalogue and observed fixture coverage

This catalogue connects 18 primary references to the existing Synexia recipe, compiler and MIndex owners. It is the documentation follow-up to the implementation and replay changes. It adds category metadata and an evidence map; it adds no dependency, search service, recipe engine or challenge implementation.

The completed donor packet contains **247 literal input pairs and 1,477 regex input pairs per native mode**. All seven donor JUnit tests passed with native mode `off`, and all seven passed again with mode `required`. The main `off` run passed 68 tests overall. The exact corpus, operations, source hashes and log hashes are in [EXECUTED_TEST_MAPPING.md](EXECUTED_TEST_MAPPING.md) and [donor_catalogue.json](donor_catalogue.json).

## Review and lookup order

1. Inventory the existing Synexia owner, its recipe and its fixtures. Record the source revision, public and private interfaces, accepted inputs, indexing, outputs and exceptions before choosing a replacement atom.
2. Consult **existing Synexia → JDK/javac/JLS → OpenRewrite → a specific GitHub donor**, in that order. JDK sources establish Java language and compiler contracts; OpenRewrite sources establish recipe behavior. A GitHub donor must fill a named gap and have a recorded file, revision and license before source adoption.
3. Classify the problem before lookup: literal or pattern grammar; full match or search; first or all occurrences; input alphabet and encoding; index coordinate; empty-input and error behavior. Look up **LeetCode → HackerRank → GeeksforGeeks**. Keep each platform's contract separate, including unavailable statement details.
4. Compare one candidate file or private atom at a time against that contract. A category match nominates a candidate. A text match alone cannot authorize an attributed Java edit. Preserve owner and overload resolution, interface shape, evaluation order and observable exceptions through the existing recipe workflow.
5. Make the reusable Maven/OpenRewrite recipe and bounded fixtures the work product. Reuse `M3RecipeMasteryCombinator` where applicable; declare finite dimensions and expected cardinality. Positive parser refusal is failure. Invalid syntax, unsupported constructs and exhausted limits are separate outcomes.
6. Retain the materialized diff, ordered lint → compile → tests → runtime evidence, and existing replay/fixed-point checks. A passing finite corpus supports its declared domain; it does not prove unrestricted equivalence or universal termination.

## Compiler, recipe and testing references

All entries are reference or API metadata. No upstream implementation is copied by this catalogue. License descriptions report the inspected source, not an adoption decision for every version.

Compilation acceptance is distinct from runtime behavior. | Public APIs through existing compiler owners; API metadata only. The seven donor tests are search/regex checks, not a new compiler implementation. |

Existing Synexia combinator drives literal products. Inspected helper header: GPL-2.0-only, no Classpath exception; helper/internal javac code not imported. |

## Problem-category references

These ten records use official problem pages or explicitly identified official supporting metadata. They contain independently written summaries; no challenge solution, editorial, statement passage or sample corpus is adopted. A category record does not mean that the corresponding challenge has been implemented.

| ID | Official problem/category | Semantic boundary | Executed application or remaining gap |

| LC-0010 | [Regular Expression Matching](https://leetcode.com/problems/regular-expression-matching/) | Restricted lowercase full-match language: dot and repetition of the preceding atom. | Restricted regex packet: 43 patterns × 31 inputs. Empty cases and `find` are explicit Synexia extensions beyond this challenge's contract. |
| LC-0044 | [Wildcard Matching](https://leetcode.com/problems/wildcard-matching/) | `?` consumes one character; wildcard `*` consumes a sequence. This differs from regex `*`. | Category only. No wildcard implementation or executed wildcard corpus in this packet. |

Empty inputs, Unicode, slice layouts and other literal operations follow Synexia contracts. |

Eleven JDK-valid unsupported/over-budget expressions are explicitly refused by the automaton. |

The executed Synexia literal contract is not represented as a verified GFG contract. |
| GFG-PARENTHESIS | [Parenthesis Checker](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/problems/parenthesis-checker2744/1) | Official indexed metadata describes bracket nesting; direct retrieval rendered a shell. | Category metadata only; no executed delimiter-language corpus in this packet. |

## Boundaries retained during comparison

| Comparison | Required distinction |
| --- | --- |
| Literal versus regex | Metacharacters are data in a literal contract. Regex grammar and quoting must be explicit. |
| Whole match versus search | Boolean `matches` and `find` are independently checked. Captures and match positions are outside this regex packet. |
| Regex versus source edit | A string containing code is still test data. Attributed source edits belong to the existing compiler/recipe fixtures. |
| UTF-16 versus UTF-8 | Character indices and byte offsets use independent oracles. Supplementary characters occupy different numbers of units. See [String](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/String.html) and [JNI string operations](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/specs/jni/functions.html#string-operations). |
| Lexical validity versus bracket balance | Java Unicode translation precedes tokenization; use the compiler and [JLS lexical rules](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se21/html/jls-3.html). |
| Java acceptance versus automaton eligibility | A valid JDK expression may exceed the automaton's supported grammar or resource bounds. Such refusal is not a passed matching case. |
| Same corpus in two modes versus new inputs | `off` and `required` are two executions of the same declared corpus. They do not double its distinct input count. |

## Provenance and unresolved checks

The source intake date is 2026-10-05. The JSON records exact URLs, retrieval method, available blob identities, reuse status and test mapping. OpenJDK's helper blob is `3d0bcfb69ebe36381c7239198f58b782e73e5102`; OpenRewrite's TypeValidation blob is `7e3be99f81f2aaf092f6a6b996d3e3158871fc24`. Most other upstream links remain floating references; bind an immutable file revision and its license before any source copying.

The JCC POM pins JUnit **5.10.2** and OpenRewrite **8.17.1**. The final catalogue rechecked the official JUnit 5.10.2 guide. Its EPL-2.0 license reference was read from the current upstream repository; an attempted historical `r5.10.2/LICENSE.md` retrieval did not yield a readable file. No dependency upgrade follows from the newer upstream documentation consulted during research.

The two unresolved GFG practice statements and the indexed-only parenthesis statement remain marked in the JSON. They cannot supply missing contracts by analogy. The earlier eight-suite, 1,871-case matrix remains an **unexecuted design proposal** and is not carried forward as executed coverage. Further regex semantics, Unicode validity, wildcard/delimiter validators, performance and wider JNI platforms remain outside the donor packet; see the explicit gaps in the executed mapping.

# Executed donor-test mapping

Both runs used the JCC verification module at `synexia-openrewrite-recipes/recipes/atom-pattern-mastery-20261005/jcc/`, which pins Java release 21, JUnit 5.10.2, OpenRewrite 8.17.1 and Surefire 3.2.5.

## Exact positive counts per mode

| Family | Logical pairs | Character representations | Character operation checks | UTF-8 slice layouts | UTF-8 text-search checks | Native-search API checks | Regex representation/operation checks |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ASCII literal | 217 | 1,337 | 6,685 | 868 | 4,340 | 868 | — |
| Scalar-Unicode literal | 30 | 180 | 900 | 120 | 600 | 120 | — |
| **Literal total** | **247** | **1,517** | **7,585** | **988** | **4,940** | **988** | — |
| Restricted regex | 1,333 | — | — | — | — | — | 13,330 |
| Structured regex | 144 | — | — | — | — | — | 1,440 |
| **Regex total** | **1,477** | — | — | — | — | — | **14,770** |

The literal owner checks first index, contains, prefix, suffix and whole literal equality: five operations per character representation or UTF-8 slice. Every literal pair checks the original `String`, an `MIndexString`, every UTF-16 composite seam, and four before/after byte-padding combinations. The padding may contain the needle outside the logical slice. An independent direct-alignment oracle computes character results; a separate byte-alignment oracle computes byte results.

Each regex pair compares `matches` and `find` with JDK `Pattern` across three character representations and two UTF-8 layouts: **10 operation checks per pair**. The positive packet requires successful compilation of all 55 declared patterns by both JDK and the automaton. It records zero parser refusals. A refused positive case fails its JUnit test.

**The 988 native-search API checks are not 988 JNI entries.** `MIndexNativeOps.indexOfBytes` can return before dispatch for empty or longer-than-input needles; native `off` uses its Java path. The tests assert the requested mode and native availability, and never change the mode property. The `required` result establishes the test result with required native availability in this environment. Regex automaton checks remain Java checks even in that run.

## Remaining coverage gaps

- The corpus is exhaustive only within its stated finite products. It does not cover every Java regex, string or software atom. Empty and Unicode literal cases are Synexia extensions beyond the cited LeetCode constraints.
- Regex capture contents, match positions, arbitrary flags, alternative line terminators, `$` final-terminator rules, vertical-tab whitespace, quantified quoted runs and class intersection are outside the positive packet. Comparison against the [JDK Pattern contract](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/util/regex/Pattern.html) remains necessary before admitting those families.
- Scalar-Unicode literal checks do not establish malformed UTF-8, isolated-surrogate, modified-UTF-8 or all Unicode behavior. Native entry instrumentation, non-byte-array dispatch forms, broader native platforms and throughput are not measured here.
- Wildcard matching, delimiter validation and the HackerRank address validator remain catalogue entries without implementations or executed corpora in this packet. GFG statement-retrieval gaps remain unresolved.
- The seven donor tests treat code-looking strings as data. They do not by themselves establish that a Java recipe preserves attribution, source outside an edit, API shape or execution behavior. Those properties belong to the existing compiler/recipe verification and its separate evidence.
- The earlier eight-suite **1,871-case proposal is unexecuted**. Its count must not be combined with these results. Repeating the donor corpus in a second mode also does not create additional distinct input cases.

# Catalogue integration and evidence epochs

This catalogue accompanies [implementation PR #9134](https://github.com/hsoliwal/com.synexia/pull/9134).
Its 18 records organize donor references and map the seven implemented donor tests to their
finite categories. It does not create a second runtime catalogue or search engine.

The authoring receipt and executed-test mapping preserve the earlier logged snapshot:
`35-final-main-tests.log` records 68 total tests with native mode off, and
`37-required-jni-donors.log` records the seven donor tests with native required. Those
immutable logs are [included with the implementation evidence](../evidence/logs/).

The subsequent complete replay on source epoch `72f6cbe0643ee046e31f144eea3413af4997d0b8`
passed 75 focused tests, eight parent tests, seven required-JNI donor tests and the
72-lane required-JNI parent test. The added seven focused tests exercise the newer host
verifier API. The two donor test files are byte-identical across these epochs; distinct
literal/regex pair counts remain 247 and 1,477 per mode. Read the
[execution evidence](../EVIDENCE.md) for source, classpath and recipe identities.

Develop advanced again during publication. The implementation PR records that concurrent
shared-transpiler integration separately. Neither this metadata nor the earlier passing
replay grants authority to overwrite those newer source changes.

## Using the catalogue in a recipe task

Start with the existing owner and its contract. Select a category, inspect the listed
primary reference, and bind the exact grammar, coordinate system, failure behavior and
source/license identity before adoption. Encode the candidate as a recipe with independent
fixtures, then use the existing compiler/JUnit/native gates to decide whether it is eligible.

The wildcard, bracket and address-validation references remain category pointers without
executed implementations in this packet. The source-retrieval gaps and floating references
are explicit in the catalogue. The earlier 1,871-case proposal is not executed evidence.

+This catalogue connects 18 primary references to the existing Synexia recipe, compiler and MIndex owners. It is the documentation follow-up to the implementation and replay changes. It adds category metadata and an evidence map; it adds no dependency, search service, recipe engine or challenge implementation.
+

+## Review and lookup order
+
+1. Inventory the existing Synexia owner, its recipe and its fixtures. Record the source revision, public and private interfaces, accepted inputs, indexing, outputs and exceptions before choosing a replacement atom.
+2. Consult **existing Synexia → JDK/javac/JLS → OpenRewrite → a specific GitHub donor**, in that order. JDK sources establish Java language and compiler contracts; OpenRewrite sources establish recipe behavior. A GitHub donor must fill a named gap and have a recorded file, revision and license before source adoption.
+3. Classify the problem before lookup: literal or pattern grammar; full match or search; first or all occurrences; input alphabet and encoding; index coordinate; empty-input and error behavior. Look up **LeetCode → HackerRank → GeeksforGeeks**. Keep each platform's contract separate, including unavailable statement details.
+4. Compare one candidate file or private atom at a time against that contract. A category match nominates a candidate. A text match alone cannot authorize an attributed Java edit. Preserve owner and overload resolution, interface shape, evaluation order and observable exceptions through the existing recipe workflow.
+5. Make the reusable Maven/OpenRewrite recipe and bounded fixtures the work product. Reuse `M3RecipeMasteryCombinator` where applicable; declare finite dimensions and expected cardinality. Positive parser refusal is failure. Invalid syntax, unsupported constructs and exhausted limits are separate outcomes.
+6. Retain the materialized diff, ordered lint → compile → tests → runtime evidence, and existing replay/fixed-point checks. A passing finite corpus supports its declared domain; it does not prove unrestricted equivalence or universal termination.

+# M3 donor catalogue and observed fixture coverage
+
+This catalogue connects 18 primary references to the existing Synexia recipe, compiler and MIndex owners. It is the documentation follow-up to the implementation and replay changes. It adds category metadata and an evidence map; it adds no dependency, search service, recipe engine or challenge implementation.
+
+The completed donor packet contains **247 literal input pairs and 1,477 regex input pairs per native mode**. All seven donor JUnit tests passed with native mode `off`, and all seven passed again with mode `required`. The main `off` run passed 68 tests overall. The exact corpus, operations, source hashes and log hashes are in [EXECUTED_TEST_MAPPING.md](EXECUTED_TEST_MAPPING.md) and [donor_catalogue.json](donor_catalogue.json).
+
+## Review and lookup order
+
+1. Inventory the existing Synexia owner, its recipe and its fixtures. Record the source revision, public and private interfaces, accepted inputs, indexing, outputs and exceptions before choosing a replacement atom.
+2. Consult **existing Synexia → JDK/javac/JLS → OpenRewrite → a specific GitHub donor**, in that order. JDK sources establish Java language and compiler contracts; OpenRewrite sources establish recipe behavior. A GitHub donor must fill a named gap and have a recorded file, revision and license before source adoption.
+3. Classify the problem before lookup: literal or pattern grammar; full match or search; first or all occurrences; input alphabet and encoding; index coordinate; empty-input and error behavior. Look up **LeetCode → HackerRank → GeeksforGeeks**. Keep each platform's contract separate, including unavailable statement details.
+4. Compare one candidate file or private atom at a time against that contract. A category match nominates a candidate. A text match alone cannot authorize an attributed Java edit. Preserve owner and overload resolution, interface shape, evaluation order and observable exceptions through the existing recipe workflow.
+5. Make the reusable Maven/OpenRewrite recipe and bounded fixtures the work product. Reuse `M3RecipeMasteryCombinator` where applicable; declare finite dimensions and expected cardinality. Positive parser refusal is failure. Invalid syntax, unsupported constructs and exhausted limits are separate outcomes.
+6. Retain the materialized diff, ordered lint → compile → tests → runtime evidence, and existing replay/fixed-point checks. A passing finite corpus supports its declared domain; it does not prove unrestricted equivalence or universal termination.
+

+

+| Whole match versus search | Boolean `matches` and `find` are independently checked. Captures and match positions are outside this regex packet. |
+| Regex versus source edit | A string containing code is still test data. Attributed source edits belong to the existing compiler/recipe fixtures. |
+| UTF-16 versus UTF-8 | Character indices and byte offsets use independent oracles. Supplementary characters occupy different numbers of units. See [String](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/String.html) and [JNI string operations](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/specs/jni/functions.html#string-operations). |

+| Java acceptance versus automaton eligibility | A valid JDK expression may exceed the automaton's supported grammar or resource bounds. Such refusal is not a passed matching case. |
+| Same corpus in two modes versus new inputs | `off` and `required` are two executions of the same declared corpus. They do not double its distinct input count. |
